best_for: Nintendo DS fans who dump their own cartridges and console firmware and want a free emulator that runs on Windows, Mac and Linux.
description:
melonDS is a Nintendo DS emulator led by the developer Arisotura, who posts project news on its website. The project turned 10 years old in November 2026.

You can map every DS button to keys or a gamepad, and set hotkeys for things only a real DS does, like closing the lid or blowing into the microphone. For games that need the mic, feed it your PC's microphone, white noise or a short WAV file. Rotate the two screens to hold the DS sideways, place them side by side, or make one larger than the other. Save states can keep your normal save file untouched. Saves are raw files that most other emulators can read, and with no game loaded you can open the DS system menu or PictoChat.

points.title: Bring your own BIOS
points.text: To boot through the DS firmware, melonDS needs `bios9.bin`, `bios7.bin` and `firmware.bin` dumped from an original DS or DS Lite. Firmware from a DSi or 3DS holds only settings and works only when you boot games directly.

points.title: DSi mode asks for more
points.text: DSi emulation needs both DSi BIOS files, a DSi firmware and a NAND image of about 240 MB. The project still lists DSi support as work in progress.

points.title: Sharper 3D on a GPU
points.text: Besides the accurate software renderer there is an OpenGL renderer that can draw 3D at higher internal resolutions. It is faster but less accurate, and work on it is what 1.2 is waiting for.

points.title: Wi-Fi is a work in progress
points.text: Local multiplayer and online connectivity are marked as work in progress, and netplay is on the to-do list, so do not count on multiplayer yet.

points.title: Free, open source, no installer
points.text: melonDS is GPLv3. Version 1.1 came out on November 18, 2025 as zip files for Windows x64 and Arm64 and a universal Mac app. Android ports exist but are unofficial and not supported by the developers.

points.title: Mac: Homebrew cask off; Linux: verified Flatpak
points.text: Homebrew disabled its cask on 2026-09-01 because the app fails Apple's Gatekeeper check. On Linux, the Flathub package for x64 and Arm64 is verified as coming from the developer.

points.title: Short history here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 3 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release.
